title: Speak a phrase: text-to-speech in a cloud function, played in the page as it came
description: A text-to-speech (TTS) API is called from a cloud function, so its key stays on the server, and the page plays what comes back. Three decisions matter. First, the key is a NAME: Secret reads GEMINI_API_KEY from the backend's secrets, the Function sends it in the x-goog-api-key header (never in the URL, which ends up in logs), and the key is never a port value the page can see. Second, and the one that is easy to get wrong: the audio an API returns today is almost always a FINISHED FILE (WAV, MP3 or OGG, with its own header, and sometimes extra chunks after the samples), so the cloud function passes the base64 and its MIME type through untouched and the page plays it as it is. Only a MIME type that says raw samples (audio/L16 or audio/pcm, which older Gemini text-to-speech returned) needs a WAV header put around it. Wrapping a finished file in a second header plays its first header as a click and anything after the samples as half a second of loud static. Gemini's current text-to-speech model returns audio/wav, so the wrap branch does not run for it. Third, failures stay readable: a script that threw answers through a failure Response with its own message, and a missing secret answers with a fixed sentence, because the Secret's own error names a server path the page should not show. Playback is a Function calling `new Audio(...)`, run from the call's Done; the call starts from a press, so the browser allows sound. In this function the value inputs have Run On Value Change unticked, because a signal runs each Function.
